title: Lauck and Pieper named to Lombardi Award midseason watch list
text:
← Back to the wire
Lauck and Pieper named to Lombardi Award midseason watch list
University of Iowa football players Trevor Lauck and Kade Pieper were named to the midseason watch list for the prestigious Lombardi Award on Oct. 14. Both athletes anchor an effective Hawkeye offensive line that has helped produce strong rushing performances this season.
University of Iowa football fourth-year offensive linemen Trevor Lauck and Kade Pieper have been named to the midseason watch list for the 2026 Lombardi Award, which is presented annually to the nation’s best college offensive or defensive lineman, according to an Oct. 14 announcement by the Lombardi committee.
Lauck, who plays left tackle, and Pieper, who plays right guard, have combined for 38 career starts. Iowa’s offensive line has rushed for over 200 yards in three games this season, including a 422-yard performance in Week 2 against Northern Iowa. This total marks the seventh-most rushing yards in a single game in program history.
In that game against Northern Iowa, the line enabled three different players to rush for more than 100 yards—a first for the program since 1983. So far this season, five Hawkeyes have achieved at least one 100-yard rushing performance, with fourth-year Kamari Moulton recording a season-best of 208 yards in Week 6 at Washington.
With Lauck and Pieper as the only two returning starters on Iowa’s offensive line, the team is averaging 31 points and 403.2 total yards per game. The Hawkeyes’ rushing attack averages 194 yards per contest while allowing just five sacks over six games.
Previous Hawkeye finalists for the Rotary Lombardi Award include center Tyler Linderbaum (2021) and defensive end Adrian Clayborn (2010). Other semifinalists from Iowa are linebacker Jay Higgins (2024), linebacker Jack Campbell (2022), offensive lineman Brandon Scherff (2014), offensive lineman Robert Gallery (2003), defensive lineman Jared DeVries (1998), offensive lineman Mike Devlin (1992), and defensive lineman Jeff Drost (1986).
No. 17 Iowa holds a record of five wins and one loss overall, and will return to action at Minnesota on Saturday, Oct. 24.
